spans.s:
Gṛtsa-mada is the name of a seer to whom the Sarvānukramaṇī attributes the authorship of the second Maṇḍala of the Rigveda. This tradition is supported by the aitareya Brāh maṇa and the aitareya Araṇyaka. The kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa speaks of him as a bhārgava, ‘descendant of bhṛgu,’ with a variant bābhrava, ‘descendant of babhru,’ but the later tradition keeps to the former patronymic. The Gṛtsamadas are often mentioned in the second Maṇḍala of the Rigveda, and are also called Śunahotras, but never Gārtsamadas or Śaunahotras, and gṛtsamada himself never occurs there.
